label: Assaf

origin.place: Israel, a stabilized cross of Awassi and East Friesian sheep

sources.text: Wikipedia (opened): the Assaf is the product of crossbreeding the Awassi and East Friesian, and it is kept in Israel. The AGRIS record was seen only as WebSearch text, not opened: it calls the Assaf a stabilized Awassi x East Friesian cross.

about.text: The Assaf is a dual-purpose sheep bred from Awassi and East Friesian stock and raised for both milk and meat. It is kept mainly in Israel, where it has become the preferred dairy sheep in place of the Awassi.

sources.text: Dual-purpose and Awassi x East Friesian origin from Wikipedia (opened). The replacement of the Awassi as Israel's preferred dairy breed is from the AGRIS record, seen as WebSearch text only.
Wikipedia (opened), citing Sheep101: a dual-purpose breed raised for both milk and meat.

facts.v: An average of 334 litres per lactation on five intensive Israeli farms; twin- and triplet-bearing ewes gave about 20 litres more (Pollott and Gootwine, 2004).
